executive_summary: SD-LEO-INFRA-VENTURE-QUALITY-CAPA-001-B closes root cause A of the chairman-ratified Venture Quality Review Programme (ratification 0afc86e4): there is no Venture Quality Model of record. Today lib/eva/quality-findings/finding-shape.js's FINDING_CATEGORIES is a hand-maintained 17-entry Object.freeze array with no generator, and lib/eva/stage-templates/analysis-steps/stage-23-launch-readiness.js's REQUIRED_CATEGORIES/ADVISORY_CATEGORIES/GROWTH_CATEGORIES are hardcoded plain-JS arrays (not a DB seed, contradicting the CAPA plan's inherited premise). This SD authors a Venture Quality Model v1 doc plus a machine-readable registry under lib/eva/quality-model/ (per dimension: owner stage, producer, reader/gate, severity policy, applicability), derives both category lists from it, and adds a two-limb CI predicate: every generated category maps to a registry dimension (blocking), and every dimension has a producer+reader or a dated waiver row (advisory at launch, with its own graduation trigger, so this does not become a new ungraduated pilot inside the SD chartered to fix ungraduated pilots). Excluded: building missing producers/readers, and changing any existing gate threshold. Verification: a live probe against the real venture_quality_findings_finding_category_check DB constraint (never a migration file header) plus a characterization test proving the derived stage-23 checklist is byte-identical to today's hand-authored one for both flag states.

functional_requirements.title: Venture Quality Model v1 doc + registry module
functional_requirements.description: Author docs/04_features/venture-quality-model-v1.md (or equivalent canonical doc location) citing chairman ratification 0afc86e4 verbatim, plus lib/eva/quality-model/registry.js: a frozen array of dimension records ({ id, name, tier, owner_stage, producer, reader_or_gate, severity_policy, applicability, ratification_pointer: {source, quote_hash} }) following the established lib/eva/config/ pattern (venture-default-capabilities.js: versioned, frozen, derived ID lists -- confirmed via Explore sub-agent discovery). Each dimension row's ratification_pointer.source is tagged chairman_verbatim | scribe_paraphrase | reconstructed; any row tagged 'reconstructed' is a BLOCKER for this FR, not a note (RISK sub-agent mitigation M-4). The chairman's own ratification text names only 5 agreement sentences and a scribe paraphrase of ~20 dimensions; the design-quality tier's published rubrics (adherence_rubrics table: design_quality_v1 = 6 dimensions, post_build_adherence_v1 = 4 dimensions = 10 total, NOT the 11 the CAPA plan's prose claims) are the only VERIFIED source for that tier -- ship v1 from those 10 published dimensions with a dated design_tier_incomplete waiver, and route the '10 vs 11' disambiguation as a narrow, non-blocking question to the chairman via Adam (RISK mitigation M-5). Do not invent the eleventh dimension in lane.
acceptance_criteria: lib/eva/quality-model/registry.js exists, exports a frozen array of dimension records, and every record has owner_stage/producer/reader_or_gate/severity_policy/applicability populated or an explicit waiver reference.
Every dimension record's ratification_pointer.source is one of chairman_verbatim|scribe_paraphrase|reconstructed; zero records are tagged reconstructed.

The design tier ships exactly the 10 dimensions verified in adherence_rubrics (design_quality_v1 + post_build_adherence_v1), each carrying a dated design_tier_incomplete waiver, not a silently-invented 11th.
A markdown doc records the model with a pointer (chairman_ratifications.id + quote_hash per ratification df3186e6), never a copied quote.

functional_requirements.title: Derive FINDING_CATEGORIES from the registry, scope-locked to that one array
functional_requirements.description: lib/eva/quality-findings/finding-shape.js's FINDING_CATEGORIES (currently Object.freeze([...17 literals]) at line 70) becomes generated from lib/eva/quality-model/registry.js instead of hand-edited. Generation is SCOPE-LOCKED to FINDING_CATEGORIES only: WARN_CAPPED_CATEGORIES (finding-shape.js:97), CAPA_001_A_BASELINE_CATEGORIES (sd-generator.js), and EXPERIENCE_REVIEW_CATEGORIES (experience-review/persist.js) stay hand-authored and are NOT regenerated from the registry (RISK mitigation M-2) -- these 3 sub-lists were each deliberately narrowed this session precisely because a shared list answered more than one question. A CI-time script probes the LIVE venture_quality_findings_finding_category_check constraint (never reads a migration file's header as a proxy for apply-state) and records each generated category's db_constraint_state; the 2 currently-known-rejected categories (feedback_widget_present, error_capture_wired -- verified via 17 live probe inserts by the RISK sub-agent) become dated waiver rows naming a follow-up ticket. This SD authors NO constraint migration.
acceptance_criteria: FINDING_CATEGORIES in finding-shape.js is generated from the registry; the generated array is order-stable and, on day one, set-equal to today's 17-entry literal (regression parity, not a silent widening or narrowing).

tests/unit/eva/quality-findings/finding-shape.test.js, vision-detectors.test.js, and any other test hard-pinning FINDING_CATEGORIES.length continue to pass unmodified (or are updated only for the generation mechanism, never the actual member count, on day one).
tests/unit/eva/experience-review/persist.test.js:72 and tests/unit/lib/eva/quality-findings/fr-c-generator.test.js:443 (guard tests for the 3 scope-locked sub-lists) remain green, UNMODIFIED.

A live-DB-constraint probe script exists, runs in CI, and both currently-rejected categories are recorded as dated waiver rows (not silently passing, not blocking on a migration this SD does not author).

functional_requirements.title: Derive stage-23 launch-readiness checklist categories from the registry
functional_requirements.description: lib/eva/stage-templates/analysis-steps/stage-23-launch-readiness.js's REQUIRED_CATEGORIES (line 61), ADVISORY_CATEGORIES (line 62), and GROWTH_CATEGORIES (line 72) become generated from the registry, reusing the ALREADY-EXISTING derivation pattern the file itself establishes for CAPABILITY_CATEGORIES (line 87: CAPABILITY_IDS.map(...) from lib/eva/config/venture-default-capabilities.js) rather than inventing a second mechanism (VALIDATION + Explore sub-agent finding). The file's own measured comment records that flattening the two default-OFF flags (LEO_S24_GROWTH_..., LEO_S24_CAPABILITY_CHECKLIST_REQUIRED) would flip EVERY in-flight venture to HOLD -- this FR must not touch that flag-conditional assembly logic, only the arrays feeding it. Stage-identity note: the file the checklist lives in is named for stage 23, but stage-24.js (line 20) is what dispatches analyzeStage23LaunchReadiness -- reference the checklist by this file/line, never by 'the stage-24 checklist' as a filename or table lookup (root cause E, owned by siblings -H/-J; this FR only needs to not make that drift worse).
acceptance_criteria: REQUIRED_CATEGORIES/ADVISORY_CATEGORIES/GROWTH_CATEGORIES are generated from the registry using the same derivation shape as the existing CAPABILITY_CATEGORIES line.

A characterization test asserts the effective checklist (categories + REQUIRED/ADVISORY split + computed verdict) is byte-identical pre/post this change, for BOTH flag states (both default-OFF, and both explicitly ON) -- proving this is a representational change, not a gate-threshold change wearing a refactor's clothes.

tests/unit/eva/stage-templates/stage-23-launch-readiness-fr1-4-6.test.js, stage-23-growth-categories.test.js, and stage-23-launch-readiness-fr3-capability-checklist.test.js continue to pass without their exact-array assertions changing member values.

functional_requirements.title: Two-limb CI predicate: category->dimension (blocking) + producer+reader-or-waiver (advisory)
functional_requirements.description: New CI workflow, path-filtered to lib/eva/quality-model/**, finding-shape.js, stage-23-launch-readiness.js, and the predicate script itself (no brace-alternation in the paths: filter -- workflow-path-filter-lint.yml blocks that shape). Limb 1 (blocking): every category emitted by FR-2/FR-3's generation maps to a registry dimension -- trivially true on day one since the categories ARE generated from the registry, but guards future drift if either generator is hand-edited later. Limb 2 (advisory, continue-on-error: true): every registry dimension has both a producer and a reader/gate, or a DATED waiver row. Limb 2 starts advisory because the programme's own root cause B (unwired producers/readers) means most dimensions fail it today; the waiver mechanism carries its own dated graduation trigger (a date after which the advisory limb is re-evaluated for promotion to blocking, recorded in the registry or a tracked follow-up ticket) so this SD's own CI check does not become a new ungraduated pilot (root cause C).
acceptance_criteria: CI job fails (blocking) when a generated category has no corresponding registry dimension.
CI job reports (non-blocking, continue-on-error) which dimensions lack a producer+reader/gate and have no dated waiver row, without failing the run.
The workflow's path filter uses explicit paths, no brace-alternation.
A dated graduation-trigger record exists (in the registry doc or a linked follow-up ticket) naming when limb 2 is reconsidered for promotion to blocking.

implementation_approach.summary: Author the model doc + registry first (pinning provenance), then generate the two existing arrays from it with regression/characterization tests proving no silent widening of scope-locked sub-lists or gate thresholds, then add the CI predicate.
steps: 1. Author the Venture Quality Model v1 doc, citing ratification 0afc86e4 verbatim, tagging each dimension's provenance (chairman_verbatim|scribe_paraphrase|reconstructed); route the '10 vs 11' design-tier question to the chairman via Adam as a narrow, non-blocking item.
2. Build lib/eva/quality-model/registry.js following the venture-default-capabilities.js pattern (frozen records, versioned, derived ID lists).
3. Generate FINDING_CATEGORIES from the registry in finding-shape.js; add the live-DB-constraint probe script; record the 2 known-rejected categories as dated waivers.

4. Generate stage-23-launch-readiness.js's REQUIRED/ADVISORY/GROWTH_CATEGORIES from the registry using the CAPABILITY_CATEGORIES derivation pattern; add the characterization test for both flag states.
5. Add the 2-limb CI predicate as a new path-filtered workflow.
